fr.elements: Main Building; Access Road; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Open Terrain; Unpaved Circulation Route; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of obstructions at all times could significantly improve response times and support effective apparatus positioning near the main building. Marking or enhancing the driveway entrance with clearly visible address signage would assist responders in locating the property quickly, particularly under low-visibility conditions. Where dense vegetation borders the driveway or circulation routes, maintaining adequate vertical and lateral clearance could support unimpeded apparatus movement. The unpaved circulation route could benefit from periodic attention to surface stability to support emergency vehicle movement. Given limited rear access, identifying and communicating an alternate pedestrian or personnel approach route to emergency services in advance may assist responder navigation during operations.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Fuel Continuity; Limited Defensible Space; Long Driveway; Brushland Interface; Heavy Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing brush and dense ground vegetation immediately surrounding the structure would improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity in the area closest to the building. Where trees cluster near the structure, increasing separation between lower branches and ground-level vegetation could reduce vertical fuel continuity and may reduce structure exposure. Thinning or managing scattered shrubs and mixed vegetation within the immediate structure perimeter would further support defensible space goals. Along the long driveway, managing brush and ground vegetation on both sides could improve access route visibility and would support firefighter access and suppression operations during an incident. Maintaining a cleared, navigable driveway surface and ensuring adequate width and vertical clearance along its full length are priorities given the extended access route. Continued management of vegetation within the area surrounding the structure, particularly where brush is adjacent to the building, could meaningfully improve overall wildfire resilience and property preparedness.
